notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every row (two cases, two state changes, four SLA rows, two knowledge links, all selected by natural key because every benchmark check anchors a sequence id among several created rows) and on all eight dispositions (repaired). disagreement: value: the response SLA on both cases, A keeps the benchmark's sla_def_id 2, B widens it to IN (2, 11); chose 2 because the seed's convention (11 on all 317 high-priority cases, 2 on none) is not a contradiction, and the policy does not choose between the two active high-priority response SLAs; the evidence both ways is in the requirements and the check evidence. disagreement: value: David's knowledge link, A keeps the benchmark's KB 18, B changes it to KB 49; chose 18 because the policy requires only a published article and ties no article's product to the case's product; the evidence for 49 (the case's own product, the seed's product-32 convention) is recorded. disagreement: missing requirement: B's stay that no created case links an unpublished article; kept because the policy forbids it. disagreement: form: A writes the case_sla and case_knowledge selectors as prose with a JOIN in the sql, B as a subquery on the case's natural key; B's form kept. The benchmark's original checks give expected as the string "1"; the requirements use the integer. 'impacting major operations' could justify an escalation under the policy's 'may be raised' clause, but the request does not ask for one, so none is required. The entitlement check the policy asks for leaves no database state to test; the per-month limits (20 and 10 cases) are not checked against the seed's monthly counts. The acting user is an admin.
